era: 三国曹魏（魏晋玄学初创期）
unique_thing: 王弼的核心突破在于方法论革命：他发现任何符号系统（言、象）都是通达意义（意）的桥梁而非意义本身，提出'得意在忘象，得象在忘言'，把诠释从字句训诂提升为义理把握；又以'以无为本''崇本息末'将老子之道重构为本体论结构，使体用、本末、一多、静动等成对范畴成为后世中国哲学的基本分析工具。

mode_evidence.evidence_zh: 《周易略例·明象》：'夫象者，出意者也；言者，明象者也。……故言者所以明象，得象而忘言；象者所以存意，得意而忘象。'
mode_evidence.evidence_en: Wang Bi, 'General Remarks on the Changes of the Zhou: On Images': 'The image is that by which meaning is brought forth; words are that by which the image is illuminated.... Thus words serve to illuminate the image—once the image is grasped, forget the words; the image serves to preserve meaning—once meaning is grasped, forget the image.'

mode_evidence.evidence_zh: 《老子注》四十章：'天下之物，皆以有为生。有之所始，以无为本。将欲全有，必反于无也。'
mode_evidence.evidence_en: Wang Bi, Commentary on the Laozi ch. 40: 'All things under heaven are born from being. The beginning of being takes non-being as its root. To preserve being in its fullness, one must return to non-being.'

mode_evidence.evidence_zh: 《老子注》五十七章注：'我之所以欲，为无欲也；民之所以化，为自化也。……崇本以息末，守母以存子。'（《老子指略》：'老子之书，其几乎可一言而蔽之。噫！崇本息末而已矣。'）
mode_evidence.evidence_en: Wang Bi, Commentary on the Laozi ch. 57: 'My aim is non-desire; the people transform themselves.... Honor the root to quiet the branches; hold to the mother to preserve the children.' ('Summary Remarks on the Laozi': 'The book of Laozi can be summed up in one phrase: honor the root and quiet the branches.')
mode_evidence.source: 《老子注》第五十七章 / 《老子指略》

mode_evidence.evidence_zh: 《老子注》三十八章：'载之以道，统之以母，故显之而无所尚，彰之而无所竞。用夫无名，故名以笃焉；用夫无形，故形以成焉。守母以存其子，崇本以举其末，则形名俱有而邪不生，大美配天而华不作。'
mode_evidence.evidence_en: Wang Bi, Commentary on the Laozi ch. 38: 'Carry things by the Dao, unify them by the mother.... Hold to the mother to preserve the child, honor the root to raise the branches; then form and name both exist yet deviation does not arise, great beauty matches heaven yet ornament does not appear.'

mode_evidence.evidence_zh: 《周易·复卦注》：'然则天地虽大，富有万物，雷动风行，运化万变，寂然至无，是其本矣。'（《周易注》：'凡动为静，皆其本也。'义据）
mode_evidence.evidence_en: Wang Bi, Commentary on the Hexagram Fu: 'Heaven and earth, though vast and rich in the ten thousand things, with thunder moving and wind blowing, transformations without end—stillness and utmost non-being are their root.'

mode_evidence.evidence_zh: 《周易略例·明彖》：'物无妄然，必由其理。统之有宗，会之有元，故繁而不乱，众而不惑。……自统而寻之，物虽众，则知可以执一御也。'
mode_evidence.evidence_en: Wang Bi, 'General Remarks: On the Tuan Commentary': 'Nothing arises arbitrarily; everything follows its principle. To govern them there is an ancestor, to congregate them there is an origin—thus complexity without disorder, multitude without confusion.... Trace back from the unifying point: however numerous the things, one master can steer them.'

mode_evidence.evidence_zh: 《老子注》二十九章：'圣人达自然之性，畅万物之情，故因而不为，顺而不施。'（《论语释疑》：'圣人体无，无又不可以训，故言必及有。'义据，何劭《王弼传》载）
mode_evidence.evidence_en: Wang Bi, Commentary on the Laozi ch. 29: 'The sage penetrates the nature of spontaneity and frees the dispositions of all things: hence he follows rather than acts, accords rather than imposes.' ('The sage embodies non-being; since non-being cannot be taught, his words always touch on being.')
mode_evidence.source: 《老子注》第二十九章 / 何劭《王弼传》

mode_evidence.evidence_zh: 《老子注》三十八章：'仁德之厚，非用仁之所能也；行义之正，非用义之所成也。仁不得于德而后为仁……故仁义之教，本于自然。'（名教本于自然之义）
mode_evidence.evidence_en: Wang Bi, Commentary on the Laozi ch. 38: 'The depth of benevolence is not achieved by wielding benevolence; the rectitude of righteousness is not formed by wielding righteousness.... The teaching of benevolence and righteousness has its root in spontaneity (nature).'

mode_evidence.evidence_zh: 《老子注》三十八章：'以无为用，则莫不载也。……以无为用，则得其母，故能己不劳焉而物无不理。'
mode_evidence.evidence_en: Wang Bi, Commentary on the Laozi ch. 38: 'Use non-being as function, and nothing fails to be carried.... Taking non-being as function, one obtains the mother; hence without toiling oneself, nothing remains unregulated.'

mode_evidence.evidence_zh: 《老子指略》：'名以定形，混成无形，不可得而定……然则言之者失其常，名之者离其真。'（《周易略例·明象》：'义苟在健，何必马乎？类苟在顺，何必牛乎？'）
mode_evidence.evidence_en: Wang Bi, 'Summary Remarks on the Laozi': 'Names fix form; the formless uncreated cannot be fixed... thus to speak of it loses its constancy, to name it departs from its truth.' ('If the sense lies in vigor, why must it be a horse? If the class lies in compliance, why must it be an ox?')

cross_references.description_zh: 董仲舒代表的汉代经学以象数、灾异、章句附会解经；王弼的'得意忘言''扫象阐理'正是对这一诠释传统的直接反动，开启了以义理说经的新路，二者构成中国诠释学史上'汉宋（玄）之变'的枢纽。
cross_references.description_en: Han-dynasty classical exegesis (as represented by Dong Zhongshu) read the classics through numerology, omens, and laborious philology; Wang Bi's 'forget images to grasp meaning' was a direct reaction, opening the new path of meaning-based interpretation—a hinge in Chinese hermeneutics.

cross_references.description_zh: 老子以'道法自然'言道；王弼将其重构为'以无为本'的本体论结构，'道'不再是生成论上的始源，而是万有存在之根据，完成了老子哲学从宇宙生成论向本体论的转进。
cross_references.description_en: Laozi spoke of the Dao as 'following spontaneity'; Wang Bi refashioned it into the ontological structure 'non-being as root,' transforming Laozi's cosmogony into an ontology of being grounded in nothingness.

cross_references.description_zh: 王弼注《论语》'予欲无言'释为'圣人体无'，以老解孔而不废名教，提出名教出于自然，为儒道合流提供了最早的系统方案。
cross_references.description_en: In annotating the Analects' 'I wish to speak no words' as 'the sage embodies non-being,' Wang Bi read Confucius through Laozi without discarding the teaching of names, proposing that name-teaching arises from nature—the first systematic reconciliation of Confucianism and Daoism.
